slides.0.title: Industry and market
slides.0.subtitle: Under 6,000 hectares, two thirds of it in one department
slides.1.title: Small and concentrated
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Scale
slides.1.highlights.0.content: INAVI's 2025 report: 1,048 registered vineyards covering 5,797.80 ha, about 20.4 million vines, worked by 676 businesses
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Canelones dominates
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Canelones has 66.77% of the area and 73.87% of the crop. Next come Montevideo (11.98%), Maldonado (7.39%), Colonia (4.75%) and San José (4.51%)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The crop
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The same report records about 87 million kg of grapes
slides.1.content: The whole country has under 6,000 ha of vines, two thirds of it in one department.
slides.2.title: The state and prices
slides.2.highlights.0.title: A minimum grape price
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Under Law 18.462 the executive sets a minimum price for wine grapes each year, after hearing INAVI on production costs
slides.2.highlights.1.title: INAVI's powers
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The same law lets INAVI set the release date of each vintage of domestic wine, the maximum yield per variety and hectare, and the minimum alcohol for sale
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Funding
slides.2.highlights.2.content: INAVI is funded by the wine promotion and control levy created by article 149 of Law 15.903; Law 18.462 adjusts it to the consumer price index every January and July
slides.2.content: Public management runs deep in Uruguay's wine market.
slides.3.title: Export and home market
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Mostly drunk at home
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Press reports citing INAVI give about 62.2 million litres of wine made in 2025, and about 4.64 million litres of bottled exports in 2024, a small share of output
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Brazil first
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The same reports: in 2024 Brazil took 54% of bottled export volume, followed by the United States at about 14%
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Where the figures come from
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The export and wine-volume figures come from press reports, with different years and definitions. This course only asks which market is largest
slides.3.content: Neighbouring Brazil is the most important export market.
